content: Privacy-friendly analytics tools (e.g. Plausible) by default strip/discard query parameters except allow-listed attribution params (utm_*, ref) rather than blocklisting sensitive ones - allow-listing is safer than blocklisting since new sensitive param names won't leak by default. Google Analytics 4 offers a data-redaction feature that pattern-matches emails and strips known-sensitive query param names, but this is opt-in and reactive (misses novel param names), reinforcing that redaction/allow-listing must happen at the analytics-call site in app code, not rely solely on the analytics vendor's backend filter.
